prompt:
Flat sumi-e ink wash painting on aged warm paper. Hand-painted, not rendered. A single isolated subject on plain paper, centred, whole subject in frame. Dark tapering brush outline, flat even ink-wash fill, uniform ambient tone with no visible light source, no cast shadow, no sheen. Monochromatic warm grey from pale paper to near-black ink. Brush character at every edge.

Subject: one of the swordsmen from the reference images, redrawn alone as a full-body FRONT VIEW for a character turnaround sheet. He faces the viewer squarely, standing upright and symmetrical, feet shoulder-width apart, both arms straight and held clearly away from the body at about 40 degrees. A lean bare-headed man, black hair tied up in a small topknot, stern plain face. A dark charcoal-grey kimono jacket with wide sleeves, crossed at the chest, and wide pleated hakama trousers in a darker ink grey, gathered above the ankles. A plain dark grey cloth sash at the waist. Dark cloth wraps on the shins, straw sandals. Everything he wears is grey ink wash: there is NO red and no other colour anywhere on him. His left hand (on the viewer's right) is open and empty. His RIGHT hand (on the viewer's left) grips a drawn katana: a plain, slightly curved steel blade with a small round guard and a wrapped hilt. The blade points down and outward, continuing the straight line of his arm, well clear of his leg, its tip a hand's width above the level of his feet. An empty dark scabbard is thrust through the sash at his left hip (the viewer's right), pointing down and back.

The references show the swordsmen fighting in a courtyard: keep their clothes, hair, build and line quality, and discard the courtyard and the fighting pose.

Plain empty paper background and nothing else in the picture: no ground line, no courtyard, no wall, no mist, no clouds, no shadow under the feet, no text, no seal. Whole figure from the top of the head to the sandals in frame with a paper margin all round.
